record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: Decide whether every search for homogeneous geodesics represented by three or more exponential factors can be reduced to a search for two-step homogeneous geodesics. A two-step homogeneous geodesic is a geodesic through o of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o with X and Y in the Lie algebra of G, and a two-step g.o. space is a homogeneous space in which every geodesic through the origin has such a representation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M = G/H, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen origin $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ denote the Lie algebra of $G$. A geodesic $\gamma$ of $M$ through $o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic if it is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, i.e. $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX) \cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$. The manifold $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ is homogeneous in this sense.

More generally, a geodesic through $o$ is called a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic if it admits a representation of the form
$$\gamma(t) = \exp(tX_1)\exp(tX_2)\cdots\exp(tX_k) \cdot o$$
for some $X_1, \ldots, X_k \in \mathfrak{g}$. In particular, a two-step homogeneous geodesic is one of the form $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$ with $X,Y \in \mathfrak{g}$, and $(M,g)$ is called a two-step g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ admits such a two-step representation.

Determine whether the following holds: for every homogeneous Riemannian manifold $(G/H, g)$ and every geodesic through $o$ that admits a $k$-step homogeneous representation with $k \geq 3$, there exist $X, Y \in \mathfrak{g}$ such that the same geodesic admits the two-step representation $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$. Equivalently, decide whether the study of $k$-step homogeneous geodesics (for $k \geq 3$) can always be reduced to the study of two-step homogeneous geodesics.
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of two-step homogeneous geodesic was introduced and developed in works on homogeneous Riemannian and Finsler manifolds, with examples and sufficient conditions established, but no result reducing the general $k$-step ($k\geq 3$) case to the two-step case appears in the literature; the question is listed among open problems in surveys on geodesic orbit spaces and remains unresolved as of available sources.

status_evidence.title: Two-step Homogeneous Geodesics in Homogeneous Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Two-step homogeneous geodesics are geodesics of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the notion of two-step homogeneous geodesic and gives sufficient conditions and examples but does not reduce higher-step geodesics to two-step ones.

status_evidence.title: Two-step homogeneous geodesics in some homogeneous Finsler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: A homogeneous Finsler manifold (G/H, F) is called a two-step homogeneous g.o. space if all geodesics have such representations.
status_evidence.claim: Studies two-step g.o. spaces in the Finsler setting; the reduction question for k>=3 is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing two-step homogeneous geodesics and three-step (or more) generalizations.
status_evidence.claim: Survey poses the reduction of higher-step geodesics to the two-step case as an open question.
